article.title: Sonam Wangchuk: The hunger striking engineer demanding Indian education reforms - BBC
article.summary: Sonam Wangchuk: The hunger striking engineer demanding Indian education reforms BBC
article.full_text: Sonam Wangchuk is a well-known Indian activist and educator who is in the headlines after going on hunger strike in support of youth-led protesters demanding reforms to the education system. At the protest site in the capital Delhi, he began fasting on 28 June and has consumed nothing but salt and water since then, losing more than 9kg. Amid concern over his rapidly deteriorating health, tensions escalated when police forcibly admitted him to hospital on 18 July. Wangchuk is protesting in support of an online satirical movement called the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) – so named after India's most senior judge used the term to describe unemployed young people. The CJP is seeking educational reforms after a series of controversies, including recent exam paper leaks. The movement is being seen as one of the biggest public displays of dissent against the government of Prime Minister Narendra Modi's which has been in power since 2014. Popularly known as "Sonam sir", Wangchuk is one of best-known public figures in the disputed Indian-administered territory of Ladakh and a well-known name in India. His work has earned international recognition, including the Ramon Magsaysay Award in 2018, often referred to as Asia's Nobel Prize. He was the inspiration for Three Idiots, the 2009 superhit Bollywood film, and in 2017, he appeared as a celebrity guest on Kaun Banega Crorepati - the Indian version of Who Wants to be a Millionaire, hosted by superstar Amitabh Bachchan. The activist's worsening health has caused alarm among his supporters. As his condition has deteriorated in the past few days, opposition leaders, activists, Bollywood actors and musicians have called on Wangchuk to end his fast. But he has said he will do so only if the government takes accountability "for the recent failures in the education system"; or if he and the CJP leadership reached parliament and MPs assured them they would take up the issue; or if lawmakers visited him in hospital and assured him this would happen. Fasting has long been woven into political life in India, a country where many of the religions its citizens embrace attach moral significance to voluntary self-denial. Wangchuk, 59, is no stranger to refusing food as a form of protest. Last year he held two hunger strikes, lasting several weeks, to highlight the fragile ecology of his hometown - an icy cold desert in the Himalayas, which is at the centre of border disputes between India and China. Before beginning his hunger strike, Wangchuk and his supporters walked for hundreds of kilometres from Ladakh to reach Delhi. They argued that more autonomy for Ladakh would help prevent exploitation of natural resources. Wangchuk and his supporters say that the fragile Himalayan ecology is in danger in the absence of constitutional safeguards. The concerns stem from the fact that the government has accelerated infrastructure development in border regions. Ladakh is strategically significant for India as it shares borders with both China and Pakistan. The federal government has sanctioned several highways, power projects and military-related infrastructure in Ladakh, which Wangchuk says will harm the region, especially in the absence of consultation with local representatives. "We don't oppose development. We want sustainable growth," he said. Wangchuk and his supporters say that Ladakh's ecology means that it can't follow the development models of other Indian states. Wangchuk has had a long career as an engineer and innovator - and has a long history of challenging the status quo. As a child, he studied for three years in the city of Srinagar (then the capital of Jammu and Kashmir state) where lessons were taught in English, Urdu and Hindi. In an interview, he recalled being the "butt of jokes" in class. "In Srinagar, I was a dumb boy from Ladakh who could not speak Hindi or English," he said. In the 1980s, his experiences led him to question the education system in Ladakh, which he said did not address local needs. He protested against the use of textbooks in English and Urdu in a region where most people spoke the Ladakhi language. "All the textbooks, even in early primary classes, came from Delhi. The examples were of unfamiliar cultures and environments like ships, oceans, coconut trees and monsoon rains," says a note on the website of a school co-founded by him. "These alien examples in alien languages only confused Ladakhi children." Since then, he has worked with local authorities and communities to ensure that the education system addresses the unique needs of children in Ladakh. Wangchuk studied mechanical engineering after a relative noticed his experiments with concave mirrors to brighten dark buildings and cook food. In recent years, he has developed a low-cost mud house that maintains a temperature of 15C even in -15C conditions. He has also designed an artificial spring in the shape of an ice stupa - a hemispherical structure common in Buddhist cultures - that stores downstream water for use during late spring when farmers need water. story.title: The Hospital Door
story.skipLabel: Sonam Wangchuk’s hunger strike for education reforms

creativeDirection.dramaticPremise: Inside a Delhi hospital, a supporter tries to save Sonam Wangchuk’s failing body, while Wangchuk turns his forced admission into one last route toward accountability for education failures.

dramaticSpine.characterGoal: Tashi wants Sonam Wangchuk to end his hunger strike immediately and accept medical care.
dramaticSpine.obstacle: Wangchuk will stop only if the government takes accountability, MPs assure the protesters they will raise the issue, or lawmakers visit him and make that assurance.
dramaticSpine.newsCatalyst: After fasting on salt and water since 28 June and losing more than 9kg, Wangchuk was forcibly admitted to hospital by police on 18 July as his health deteriorated.
dramaticSpine.reversal: The hospital, which feels like the end of the protest, becomes one of the places where lawmakers could still reach him and give the required assurance.
dramaticSpine.costOfFailure: His worsening health continues while the education reform demands remain unanswered.
dramaticSpine.emotionalTurn: Tashi stops treating the hospitalisation only as defeat and accepts the risk of carrying Wangchuk’s demand beyond the room.
dramaticSpine.resolution: Tashi leaves to seek the promised political assurance, while Wangchuk chooses to continue the fast for now.

visualBible.setting: A quiet Delhi hospital room immediately after a police-forced admission, with a narrow bed, IV stand, window haze, and a folded protest shawl brought from the demonstration site.
visualBible.colorAndLighting: Muted saffron, blue and dusty-white hospital tones; harsh afternoon Delhi light through blinds gradually softens into a warmer, intimate glow.
recurringProps: plain metal water cup containing salt water
visualBible.storyArc: The room begins as a place of confinement and medical alarm, then becomes a charged crossroads: Tashi leaves to seek lawmakers while Wangchuk remains still, holding his line.
visualBible.referenceImagePrompt: Editorial animated-film still of Sonam Wangchuk, a 59-year-old Indian Ladakhi engineer and educator with silver hair, trimmed grey beard, rectangular glasses and a blue woollen shawl, lying in a Delhi hospital bed beside Tashi, a fictional young Ladakhi supporter in a faded brown jacket; salt-water cup, cloth bag and IV stand visible; dusty afternoon light through blinds, intimate tense mood, cinematic 2D-3D animation, upper-third space clear for captions, no text, logos, or watermark.

cast.role: Sonam Wangchuk, engineer and educator on hunger strike
cast.voiceProfile: Warm, weathered male voice with quiet Ladakhi steadiness; slow, breath-conscious pace and restrained humour at the start, becoming firmer and more tender by the ending, with meaningful pauses that suggest physical weakness without melodrama.
cast.visualIdentity: Silver hair, trimmed grey beard, rectangular glasses, pale hospital clothing, blue woollen shawl, visibly tired but alert.

cast.role: Tashi, fictional young supporter from the protest
cast.voiceProfile: Young adult voice with close-mic urgency, quick nervous pace and contained frustration; interrupts gently at first, then shifts into determined warmth and focused resolve by the final line.
cast.visualIdentity: Young Ladakhi supporter in a faded brown jacket, canvas shoes, hospital visitor badge, anxious eyes and a small cloth bag.

beats.dramaticAction: Tashi catches Wangchuk’s hand as he reaches for the salt-water cup in the hospital bed.
beats.turningPoint: Wangchuk’s hunger strike is no longer only at the protest site; the hospital room makes his physical decline unavoidable.

visual.caption: Sonam Wangchuk’s hunger strike for education reforms
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film close shot: Tashi catches Sonam Wangchuk’s wrist beside a salt-water cup as he lies in a Delhi hospital bed; blue shawl, silver hair, glasses, IV stand, cloth bag, dusty afternoon light, handheld-feeling camera, tense intimate mood, clear upper-third caption space, no text, logos, or watermark.
visual.scenePrompt: Continuous opening shot in the same hospital room: begin on the trembling cup, then tilt to Tashi stopping Wangchuk’s hand.
visual.continuityNotes: Establish Wangchuk’s blue shawl, Tashi’s brown jacket, salt-water cup and IV stand; nothing changes except Tashi’s grip.

lines.speaker: tashi
lines.text: Sonam sir, this is Wangchuk’s hunger strike—and you’re in hospital now. Please, stop.

lines.speaker: sonam
lines.text: Since 28 June, only salt and water. I cannot pretend the demand disappeared with the bed.

beats.dramaticAction: Tashi lifts the cup away, then hesitates when Wangchuk’s weak hand reaches after it.
beats.turningPoint: The small act of protection becomes a conflict: saving him physically may mean ending the protest before its conditions are met.

visual.caption: The protest follows him into the ward
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film medium shot: Tashi pulls the plain salt-water cup toward his chest while Wangchuk reaches weakly from the bed; IV tubing, blue shawl, hospital blinds and cloth bag remain visible, sharp side light, anxious mood, upper-third space clear for captions, no text, logos, or watermark.
visual.scenePrompt: Continue without a cut in emotional time: Tashi steps between the bed and the cup, trying to sound firm while Wangchuk watches him.
visual.continuityNotes: Cup moves from the bedside to Tashi’s hands; Wangchuk remains propped up, and the blue shawl stays over his shoulders.

lines.speaker: tashi
lines.text: You’ve lost more than nine kilos. People are asking you to end this.

lines.speaker: sonam
lines.text: I will, if accountability comes—or MPs assure us they will take the education failures up.

beats.dramaticAction: A hospital door opens off-screen; Tashi turns sharply, but no lawmaker appears, and he sets the cup back down.
beats.turningPoint: The forced admission that looked like the protest’s defeat reveals a possible route: lawmakers can still come to him in hospital.

visual.caption: Police took him to hospital on 18 July
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film over-shoulder shot from behind Tashi as the hospital door opens into a bright corridor, empty of visitors; Wangchuk remains in bed, salt-water cup returned to the table, blue shawl and IV stand fixed, stark white light against the dim room, suspenseful mood, upper-third space clear for captions, no text, logos, or watermark.
visual.scenePrompt: The camera tracks Tashi’s sudden turn toward the opening door, then settles back on Wangchuk as the corridor stays empty.
visual.continuityNotes: The cup returns to the table; preserve the same bed position, shawl, IV stand and cloth bag. The open doorway is the only new element.

lines.speaker: tashi
lines.text: Police forcibly brought you here on 18 July. That was supposed to end the danger.

lines.speaker: sonam
lines.text: Or change the doorway. Lawmakers can visit me here and assure us they’ll take it to Parliament.

beats.dramaticAction: Tashi grabs the cloth bag and moves toward the door, then stops to look back at Wangchuk’s exhausted face.
beats.turningPoint: Tashi must choose between staying to guard Wangchuk and leaving to pursue the political assurance that could end the fast.

visual.caption: The hospital becomes the next battleground
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film wide shot: Tashi grips the small Ladakh cloth bag near the hospital door, looking back at weak but resolute Wangchuk in bed; blue shawl, salt-water cup, IV stand, slatted Delhi light, dramatic diagonal composition, conflicted mood, generous upper-third caption space, no text, logos, or watermark.
visual.scenePrompt: Continue as Tashi crosses the room in three hurried steps, then freezes at the threshold while Wangchuk remains motionless.
visual.continuityNotes: Tashi now holds the cloth bag and stands at the door; Wangchuk’s cup and shawl remain unchanged, preserving the room’s visual anchor.

lines.speaker: tashi
lines.text: The CJP wants reforms after the exam paper leaks. I should find the MPs.

lines.speaker: sonam
lines.text: Go. If they come here, I can listen. If not… I remain where they put me.

beats.dramaticAction: Tashi opens the door and leaves; Wangchuk turns the salt-water cup slightly away, choosing not to drink it.
beats.turningPoint: Tashi accepts the risk of leaving, while Wangchuk makes his immediate choice clear: the fast continues until one of the promised assurances arrives.

visual.caption: One leaves to seek an answer; one stays with the demand
visual.imagePrompt: Editorial animated-film final shot: Tashi exits through the hospital door with the cloth bag, while Wangchuk gently turns the salt-water cup away on the bedside table; blue shawl, IV stand, warm fading Delhi light, quiet determined mood, upper-third space clear for captions, no text, logos, or watermark.
visual.scenePrompt: Hold on Wangchuk after Tashi disappears; the door clicks softly, and the camera rests on the untouched cup and his steady gaze.
visual.continuityNotes: Carry forward every prop and position from the previous shot. Advance only the open door closing, Tashi’s absence and Wangchuk’s deliberate refusal.

lines.speaker: tashi
lines.text: I’ll bring back an assurance—or bring the lawmakers themselves.

lines.speaker: sonam
lines.text: Then I’ll wait. Salt, water… and the door.

story.exit: The door closes on Tashi’s hurried search, while Wangchuk remains in the hospital room, his immediate choice—and the cost of it—held in the untouched cup.
